page.layout: One page of text, one column, with a running head at the top. Below it, a decorative fleuron, then a centred chapter heading with a subtitle, a woodcut-initialled italic summary, and the body text in paragraphs. No marginal notes, no footnotes.

main_text.p: bus, veluti Ambrosio, Chrysostomo & Basilio in Exameris, sed tamen in hominis anima, non in corpore semper ab iis posita est imago Dei in homine. Quid sit autem illa, & qualis, explicat Paulus Coloss. 4. verf. 10. Ephes. 4. verf. 24. nec melior interpres quærendus erat. Ergo ad Anthropomorphitas istos refero, & ad eorum tempora. Huius hæresis meminit Isidor. lib. 8. etymologiar.
main_text.head: CAP. LXXVII. Opheorum error quis fuerit.

head.i: Alia dicit innumerabiles mundos, sicut opinati sunt quidam philosophi gentium.

main_text.p: I Innumerabiles mundos.)In indice præposito huic operi vocantur Ophei qui hoc delirium amplexi sunt, siue quòd ab Ophitis hæreticis orti sunt, siue quòd Opheus quidam eorū author fuerit, quos tamen à Valentinianis & Basilidianis potius ortos esse iudico, qui 365. cœlos constituunt. Quid enim facilius fuit, quàm post cœlorum globos inductos facere mundos innumerabiles? Quod autea[?] ab ethnicis philosophis traditum erat, quemadmodum à Democrito Abderita, & Epicuro Atheniensi. Id quod in eorum vita refert Diogenes Laertius, libr. 9. & 10. Lactant. De ira Dei. cap. 10. Origenes quidem libr. 3. περὶ ἀρχῶν[?], cap. 5. opinatur præter hunc visibilem & conspicuum mundum, alium quoque

page.notes: The woodcut initial "A" of the italic summary is decorative; read as "Alia" with [?]. "autea" is printed as such and probably stands for "autem"; left as printed with [?]. The Greek "περὶ ἀρχῶν" after "libr. 3." is small and partly blurred; accents read with [?]. The ")" after "mundos." is printed as shown. The page ends mid-sentence ("alium quoque"), continued on the next page.
